correctness.rationale: For each n the explicit firing counts (3d−1,d) on the left and (3d,d) on the right, with parity-dependent vertex-zero counts, give a conservation vector leaving one chip at c=ceil(n/2), and terminal rotor arrows form a single c–c-leaf cycle. A first-excess-firing argument bounds actual counts by the certificate; zero discrepancy outside a deficient set makes that set rotor-closed, contradicting all terminal arrows outside c flowing to c. Thus the actual first hit of c has exactly the predicted sum n²−ceil(n/2). Before that hit, chip cannot belong to the frozen c↔c-leaf cycle, so is not recurrent; on hitting, the terminal unicycle criterion proves recurrence. Independent direct simulation for n=3,4,5,6,7,8,10,20,50 reproduces times 7,14,22,33,45,60,95,390,2475; these samples are not the all-n proof. Upper bound invokes known general O(|E|diam) lock-in, not a claimed exact all-state maximum.
